purpose: Plan 9 rc compatibility matrix for Star 9

crate_boundary.rule: The reusable rc crate has no dependency on Star 9 runtime, web, CLI, or browser glue.

features.notes: Typed AST covers simple commands, assignments, blocks, parenthesized groups, functions, if/if not across command separators, Plan 9 service-address words such as tcp!host, for/while/switch, pipelines, boolean operators, redirection, process substitution, here documents, and command substitution words.
Supports list assignments, empty lists, positional args, $name, $#name, $"name, subscripts, rc apostrophe quoting, doubled apostrophes, and caret concatenation.
Implements *, ?, character classes, complemented classes, ranges, unmatched literal preservation, and the ~ builtin over host filesystem listings.

Supports sequencing, &&, ||, !, deterministic background jobs, wait reporting, wait <job>, if, for, while, switch, functions, and rc-style status strings including all-zero pipeline success. The Star 9 adapter now materializes background graph records as task entries; true task-group scheduling remains host-limited.

Implements <, >, >>, fd-specific output redirects, fd dup/close for captured stdout/stderr, /dev/null handling, stdout/stderr pipe selection, <{} and >{} process substitution through evaluator pipes, and parsed here documents with quoted-delimiter expansion suppression. The reusable evaluator remains deterministic; the Star 9 adapter now creates observable task/fd graph records for pipelines and process substitution. Concurrent streaming external stage execution remains host-limited.
Backquote braced command substitution runs through the evaluator and splits output with ifs.

Variables, local command assignments, zero-byte-separated environment export/import, fn#name function export/import, sigexit, and deliver_note(sig*) hooks are implemented in the reusable evaluator. Star 9 mounts a runtime #env/env device and the rc adapter imports/exports rc variables and functions through that file surface.

Implements core builtins including ., basename, cd, echo, eval, exec, exit with sigexit, shift, status, test, wait, whatis, ~, true, false, explicit builtin dispatch, stable flag behavior, and host-routed rfork. Exact rfork namespace/env/fd/process sharing beyond supported flags remains host-limited.

External command execution is a host-trait operation. The reusable evaluator searches $path for rc scripts, sets $0/$*, and dispatches wasm/js-looking namespace files back to the host. The Star 9 adapter maps .wasm/.wat through wasi and .js/.mjs through worker while preserving deterministic opt-in host execution behavior.

Native `star9 rc`, rc-first `star9 shell`, wasm `createRcShell`, and rc-first `<star9-shell>` are wired. The smaller admin parser remains available as `star9 shell --simple` and `<star9-shell simple>`.

The Star 9 adapter can run shell-visible `bind`, source-specific `unmount`, `srv`, and `mount` commands through namespace/service files. Loopback services are implemented by default; native hosts can register tcp!host!port 9P services when explicitly used. Browser shell services support import!/MessagePort sources. Disk and vac providers return precise provider-missing errors until corresponding Star 9 providers are configured.
Optional STAR9_RC_ORACLE comparison runs only when configured and compares portable stdout, stderr, and status cases against plan9port or 9front rc.
